sections.h2: Who sends a Bismarck property tax bill
sections.html:
Burleigh County sends the bill, and the City of Bismarck sets the value. The city's Assessing Division values property inside city limits. The Burleigh County Auditor/Treasurer mails the statement, collects the money and passes it to the taxing districts each month.

In Bismarck the county controls less than 13 percent of the total bill. The rest goes to the city, the school district and other local districts, and the county has no authority over those levies. If a bill looks high, ask the city assessor about the value or the district about its levy, not the treasurer.

The county's office is at 221 N 5th Street, Bismarck, ND 58501, phone 701-222-6718. The mailing address is PO Box 5518, Bismarck, ND 58506.

Bismarck is North Dakota's capital and the seat of Burleigh County, on the east bank of the Missouri River across from Mandan. The 2020 census counted 73,622 residents, and the 2024 estimate is 77,772. State government, health care and the schools are the biggest employers, which gives sellers a steady pool of local buyers.

Winters are long and snowy, so buyers look closely at roofs and heating systems. If a home sits near the river or a creek, check its flood map status before you sell, since the upper Missouri still floods seasonally.

sections.h2: How the tax bill is calculated
sections.html:
North Dakota multiplies taxable value by the combined mill levy. The assessor sets market value, called true and full value. Assessed value is 50 percent of that, and taxable value is 9 percent of assessed value for residential property and 10 percent for commercial and agricultural property.

The county's 2025 mill levy sheet lists a total of 237.10 mills for the City of Bismarck taxing district. Multiply your taxable value by that levy to estimate the consolidated tax before any credits or state-paid relief, then compare the result with your statement.

Special assessments for streets, sidewalks and water and sewer lines are billed on the same statement. They usually run several years and include principal on the borrowing, so a seller with a long balance should ask the title company how it will be handled.

Real estate tax is due January 1 and is payable without penalty until March 1. A 5 percent discount applies if the full bill, specials included, is paid by February 15. Statements are mailed in December, and state law requires mailing by December 26.

March 23%

The second installment, due October 15, takes a 6 percent penalty on October 16. You can pay online through the county's property search, by phone at 1-800-272-9829 with jurisdiction code 4434, or by mail to the Burleigh County Auditor. E-checks cost $3.98 under $10,000 and $19.92 at $10,000 or more. Cards cost 3.61 percent with a $1.52 minimum. A postmark on or before the deadline counts for the 5 percent discount, but the county does not guarantee mail delivery.

Start with the city's Assessing Division at 701-355-1630, then use the boards of equalization. The city board must meet in the first 15 days of April, and the county board meets in June. The State Board meets the second Tuesday of August, and you must have appeared before the city and county boards to reach it.

Both local boards meet at 221 N 5th Street, and the city must mail written notice within 15 days after a board raises a value.

If you miss the boards, you can file for abatement with the county auditor under N.D.C.C. 57-23-04. The deadline is November 1 of the year after the tax becomes delinquent.

Property becomes subject to foreclosure of the tax lien if taxes, specials and penalties stay unpaid into the third year. The county then follows a set calendar:

  • Before June 1: notice of foreclosure goes to owners and occupants.
  • Before August 1: the delinquent list is published in the official county newspaper.
  • October 1: the tax lien foreclosure date, with payment in full due by 5 p.m.
  • Third Tuesday of November: the annual tax sale.

You can bring the account current any time before the sale starts. The county posts sale notices at least 15 days ahead and publishes them at least 10 days ahead. Ask the treasurer for a payoff figure that includes interest.

The county's Tax Equalization office lists several programs. Check each against current rules before applying:

  • Homestead credit for owners 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled, with an income limit the county lists as under $70,000
  • Disabled veteran credit for an honorable discharge and a VA rating of 50 percent or more
  • Exemptions for wheelchair use, blindness and paraplegic disabled veterans
  • Farm residence exemption, which needs a statement of farm gross income

Each program has an application deadline, so call 701-222-6693 to confirm what is open before you rely on one.

The title company pays unpaid property tax and any special assessment balance from your sale proceeds at closing. You do not have to find the money first. You do need a payoff figure from the Burleigh County Auditor/Treasurer, which should include penalties up to the closing date. City specials are paid through the City of Bismarck Special Assessments Department.

A cash buyer purchases the house as-is, so liens for taxes are simply part of the closing statement.

1. Call 701-222-6718 for the payoff on taxes and specials.
  2. Ask the city whether special assessments run beyond the sale date.
  3. Check the board calendar if you plan to dispute the value.
  4. Confirm any credit you hold, such as the homestead credit, and tell the title company.

With these four answers in hand, the closing statement holds few surprises, and a buyer's lender will see a clean tax record.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to in Bismarck, ND?
faqs.a: You pay Burleigh County. The county auditor/treasurer's office at 221 N 5th Street collects the tax, and the City of Bismarck's Assessing Division sets the value.

faqs.q: What is the Bismarck property tax discount?
faqs.a: A 5 percent discount applies to the consolidated tax if the whole bill, including specials, is paid by February 15.

faqs.q: When does a Bismarck tax bill become late?
faqs.a: The first installment is payable without penalty until March 1. A 3 percent penalty starts March 2 and rises to 12 percent on October 15. The second installment takes 6 percent after October 15.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Bismarck assessment after the April meeting?
faqs.a: Yes, through abatement. File with the county auditor by November 1 of the year after the tax becomes delinquent, under N.D.C.C. 57-23-04.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bismarck house that has unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax and specials are paid from the proceeds at closing, so ask the county for a payoff figure before you sign.
